text:
maya: Heads up — this morning we saw a burst where CA spun up 4 GPU nodes for a training batch, then scaled them down within ~90s. Jobs started getting OOM/restarts and we burned spot credits. Anyone seen this pattern?

tonY: I saw the cloud metrics, scale-up is fine but scale-down looks aggressive. CA default `--scale-down-unneeded-time` is 10m, so it shouldn't drop that fast. Could be `max-empty-bulk-delete` or some predicate failing.

maya: I'm pretty sure the pods were pending on GPU nodepool and then bound, so CA scaled. But then a DaemonSet/metrics-proxy landed and kept small allocatable CPU, CA considered nodes unneeded? Weird.

sasha: Quick checklist: 1) Are there PDBs or DaemonSets preventing eviction? 2) Are GPU pods using `BestEffort` or tiny requests so utilization thresholds mark nodes unneeded? 3) CA version? Newer CA changed `balance-similar-node-groups` behavior.

alex: For what it's worth, we hit a similar case where `kube-proxy` and our `node-exporter` DS reduced available resources on fresh nodes and CA's `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` thought node was idle. We solved by bumping `--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.6` and `--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m`.

maya: Trying that in staging. Also thinking of `--max-node-provision-time` bump — sometimes cloud take too long and CA gives up and then wrong decisions occur.

tonY: Another leaky pattern: if trainer pods request very small CPU but GPUs are huge, CA's binpacking/expander picks nodes that look underutilized by CPU. Consider `--expander=least-waste` vs `random`. least-waste helps pack GPU-only workloads.

maya: Good call. Current expander is `priority`. We can try `least-waste` for the GPU nodepool.

ella-oncall: Adding note: this mostly affects spot-backed GPU pools in us-west-2 during morning batch window. Could be churn from autoscaler mixed with spot termination events. I opened infra ticket: https://go.redwood/infra/issue/4123 (infra-bot created).

infra-bot: issue 4123 created by ella-oncall: "gpu-pool-flap-scale-down-investigation"

alex: Also check `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false` (we have it true?). If it's true CA skips nodes with DaemonSets and will avoid deleting them — but when set incorrectly you get flips.

sasha: We should also look at `--scale-down-unready-time` for nodes that are NotReady during kubelet start. Set to `20m` if kubelet takes long to register.

maya: Proposed quick changes in staging: 
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m
--scale-down-unready-time=20m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.6
--expander=least-waste
--max-empty-bulk-delete=1
```
I'll apply as a canary to the GPU autoscaler group and watch for flaps.

tonY: Also consider adding a tiny guaranteed CPU request to our GPU trainer pod (e.g., `cpu: 100m`) so CA doesn't think the node is empty immediately. That reduces false-positive unneeded.

maya: Nice — will add that to the kustomize overlay for training jobs.

ella-oncall: If the canary looks good, let's roll to production after 24h of normal behaviour. Also prepare rollback plan (revert flags & scale-down settings).

maya: Running the canary now. I pushed a change to k8s/autoscaler/gpu-ca-helm -> chart revision `v1.3.8-canary1`. Will paste results in ~30m.

alex: If this persists, we might need to enable `balance-similar-node-groups` off or on depending on node group similarity — we've seen CA bounce between similar groups and cause churn.

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:"
